text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a librarian.
script: W: Hi, I'm looking for a book about marine biology, but the computer says it's checked out.
M: Let me see. Yes, someone borrowed it last week. It's due back on Friday.
W: Oh no. I need it for a report that's due Monday.
M: Well, I can place a hold for you. We'll send you an email as soon as it's returned.
W: That would be great. Is there anything else on the same topic?
M: There's a newer book on the second floor, in the science section. It's about ocean animals.
W: Perfect. I'll go look at it now. Thanks for your help.
M: You're welcome. Just bring it to this desk when you're ready to borrow it.

stem: Why does the student talk to the librarian?
options: She wants to return a late book to the library desk.
She needs a book that is not available now.
She wants to join a science club on campus.
She needs help using a library computer.
explanation: The student says the marine biology book 'is checked out' and she needs it for a report. So she wants a book that is currently unavailable. She does not mention returning a book; the librarian only says someone else's copy is due on Friday.

stem: What will the student probably do next?
options: The first copy will be returned today, so she will wait at the desk for it.
She will go and find a newer book on the second floor.
She will go home and start writing her report.
She will ask another student to lend her the book.
explanation: The librarian says 'There's a newer book on the second floor,' and the student answers 'I'll go look at it now.' She will not wait at the desk, because the first book is not due back until Friday.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a housing office worker.
script: W: Housing office, how can I help you?
M: Hi, I live in Maple Hall, room 214. My heater isn't working, and it's really cold at night.
W: I'm sorry to hear that. How long has it been broken?
M: Since Sunday. I put a note in the online system, but nobody came.
W: Let me check. Oh, I see your request here. It looks like the repair team is busy this week.
M: Could someone come tomorrow? I have an exam on Thursday, and I can't study when I'm freezing.
W: I'll mark it as urgent. Someone should visit your room tomorrow morning.
M: Thank you so much. I'll make sure I'm there.

stem: What problem does the man have?
options: His room is too noisy for him to study in at night.
He lost the key to his room in the building.
The heating in his room does not work.
He was given the wrong room by the office.
explanation: The man says 'My heater isn't working, and it's really cold at night.' The other problems are never mentioned.

stem: What does the woman agree to do?
options: Ask for the repair to be done sooner.
Move the man into a warmer building next week.
Send him a new heater to use today.
Fix the heater herself tomorrow morning.
explanation: She says 'I'll mark it as urgent. Someone should visit your room tomorrow morning.' She does not offer a new room or repair it herself; the repair team will come.

text: Listen to a conversation between two students in a cafeteria.
script: M: Hey, Priya. Is this seat taken?
W: No, go ahead. How was your biology test?
M: Honestly, it was harder than I expected. I studied all weekend, but the last section was tricky.
W: Oh, I'm sorry. I have mine tomorrow, and I'm nervous.
M: Do you want to study together after lunch? I could share my notes.
W: That would really help. I have a class until two, though.
M: No problem. Let's meet at the library at two thirty.
W: Great. I'll bring my flash cards, and we can quiz each other.

stem: What are the speakers mainly discussing?
options: Choosing a class for next term.
Preparing for a test.
Planning a weekend trip.
Finding a place to eat lunch.
explanation: They talk about the man's biology test and the woman's test tomorrow, and they plan to study together. Lunch is only the setting.

stem: When will the speakers meet?
options: Before the woman's class starts.
On Saturday morning.
After the woman's class ends.
Right after the man's test.
explanation: The woman has a class until two, and the man suggests 'two thirty' at the library. So they will meet after her class. Nothing is said about the weekend.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a professor.
script: W: Come in, Hamza. What can I do for you?
M: Thanks for seeing me, Professor. I wanted to ask about the final paper.
W: Of course. Have you chosen a topic yet?
M: I'm thinking about writing on renewable energy, but I'm not sure it's specific enough.
W: It's a bit broad. Maybe you could focus on solar power in cities.
M: Oh, that's a great idea. Would it be okay to interview someone from the campus energy office?
W: Absolutely. In fact, I know the manager. I'll send her an email and introduce you.
M: That would be wonderful. Thank you.

stem: Why does the student visit the professor?
options: To ask for a higher grade on his last paper.
To find out the date and time of the final exam.
To borrow a book about energy from her shelf.
To get advice about a paper topic.
explanation: He says 'I wanted to ask about the final paper' and asks whether his topic is specific enough. He does not ask about grades or exams.

stem: What does the professor offer to do?
options: Email a person who can help him.
Read the whole paper before it is due.
Give him extra time to finish the paper.
Choose a topic for him this week.
explanation: She says 'I'll send her an email and introduce you' about the campus energy office manager. She suggests a narrower topic but does not choose it for him.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a bookstore clerk.
script: W: Excuse me, I bought this textbook yesterday, but it's the wrong edition.
M: Let me take a look. Oh, this is the ninth edition. What does your syllabus say?
W: It says the tenth edition. I should have checked more carefully.
M: That's okay. Do you have your receipt?
W: Yes, here it is.
M: Great. Since it's within seven days, I can give you a full refund or exchange it.
W: I'd like to exchange it, please. Do you have the tenth edition in stock?
M: We do. It costs a little more, though. You'll need to pay the difference.
W: That's fine.

stem: What is the student's problem?
options: She lost the receipt for her purchase.
She bought an old edition of the book.
The book costs too much for her budget.
The store has no copies of the book left.
explanation: She says 'it's the wrong edition' and her syllabus requires the tenth, while she has the ninth. She does have her receipt, and the clerk says the right book is in stock.

stem: What does the student decide to do?
options: Get her money back.
Keep the book and borrow another one.
Exchange the book and pay extra.
Come back with her teacher.
explanation: She says 'I'd like to exchange it,' and the clerk explains she must pay the difference. A refund was offered, but she chose the exchange.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a member of the hiking club.
script: W: Hi, I saw your poster about the hiking club. Is it too late to join?
M: Not at all. We welcome new members all semester. Have you hiked before?
W: A little, but only short trails near my hometown.
M: That's fine. Our trips are for all levels. This Saturday we're going to the lake, and it's an easy walk.
W: That sounds nice. Do I need to bring anything special?
M: Just comfortable shoes, water, and a lunch. The bus leaves from the main gate at eight.
W: Eight in the morning? Okay, I'll set an alarm. How much does it cost?
M: The membership is ten dollars, and you can pay on the bus.

stem: Why does the woman talk to the man?
options: She wants to complain about a poster that is wrong.
She wants to borrow equipment for a long trail.
She wants to find out how to join the club.
She wants to plan a trip to her hometown.
explanation: She asks 'Is it too late to join?' The rest of the talk is about how the club works and what to bring. The poster is only how she heard about the club.

stem: What does the man say about the Saturday trip?
options: It is suitable for beginners.
It is a long and difficult hike for experienced walkers.
It begins in the afternoon after the club meeting.
It is free for everyone who brings their own lunch.
explanation: He says 'Our trips are for all levels' and 'it's an easy walk.' The bus leaves at eight in the morning, and membership costs ten dollars, so the other choices are wrong.

text: Listen to a conversation between an intern and her supervisor.
script: M: Amara, do you have a minute? I wanted to talk about your first week.
W: Sure. I hope I'm doing okay.
M: You're doing very well. The marketing team says your social media ideas are creative.
W: Thank you. I've enjoyed it, but I'm still learning the software.
M: That's normal. In fact, there's a training session on Wednesday afternoon. I'd like you to attend.
W: I'd love to. Is it okay if I leave my desk for two hours?
M: Of course. And afterwards, we'll give you your own project. It'll be a small campaign for the spring sale.
W: Wow, that's exciting. I can't wait to start.

stem: What is the main purpose of the supervisor's talk with Amara?
options: To ask her to stay late on Wednesday.
To discuss how she is doing at work.
To tell her the internship is ending soon.
To explain how to use the company software.
explanation: He says 'I wanted to talk about your first week' and then praises her work and plans training. The training is on Wednesday afternoon, but he does not ask her to stay late.

stem: What will Amara probably do after the training?
options: Teach the marketing team how to use social media.
Ask for a longer internship with the company.
Work on a small campaign by herself.
Write a report about the training session.
explanation: The supervisor says 'afterwards, we'll give you your own project... a small campaign for the spring sale.' The other actions are never suggested.

text: Listen to a conversation between two roommates.
script: W: Lucas, can we talk about the kitchen? There were dirty dishes in the sink again this morning.
M: Oh, sorry. I had a late practice last night and I was too tired to wash them.
W: I understand, but it's been happening a lot this week.
M: You're right. Maybe we should make a schedule, so we each have days to clean.
W: I was thinking the same thing. How about I take Monday, Wednesday, and Friday?
M: That sounds fair. I'll do the other days, and we can both clean on Sunday.
W: Perfect. I'll write it on the whiteboard by the fridge.
M: Thanks for being patient with me.

stem: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Buying new dishes for the apartment.
Paying the rent on time each month.
Finding a quieter place to sleep.
Sharing the kitchen cleaning.
explanation: Sofia complains about dirty dishes, and they agree on a cleaning schedule. Money and noise are not discussed.

stem: What does the man mean when he says 'Thanks for being patient with me'?
options: He wants to change his practice time.
He knows he should have helped more.
He thinks the woman is too slow at cleaning.
He plans to move out of the apartment soon.
explanation: He has just agreed that he left dishes undone, and he thanks her for waiting for him to change. This shows he knows the problem was partly his fault.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a train station employee.
script: W: Excuse me, I need to get to the city airport. Which train should I take?
M: You can take the blue line, but you'll need to change at Central Station.
W: Is there a direct train? I have two big suitcases.
M: There's an airport express, but it only runs every hour. The next one leaves at four fifteen.
W: What time is it now?
M: Almost four. So you only have a short wait.
W: Then I'll take the express. How much is a ticket?
M: Twelve dollars. You can buy it at the machine over there, or I can sell you one here.
W: I'll buy it from you, please. Machines always confuse me.

stem: What does the woman want to know?
options: How to travel to the airport.
Where to leave her heavy suitcases.
When the station will close tonight.
How much a taxi to the city costs.
explanation: Her first words are 'I need to get to the city airport. Which train should I take?' Her suitcases are the reason she wants a direct train, not the question itself.

stem: Why does the woman choose the airport express?
options: It is much cheaper than the blue line.
It leaves from a platform near the machine.
It needs no change of trains.
It runs every few minutes through the day.
explanation: She asks for a direct train because she has two big suitcases, and the express is direct. The express runs only every hour, so the last choice is wrong, and the price is not compared.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a gym worker.
script: W: Welcome to the campus gym. Are you here for a tour?
M: Yes, I just started classes, and I'd like to join.
W: Great. Students get a discount. You'll pay twenty dollars a month if you show your student card.
M: That's cheaper than I thought. What's included?
W: You can use the weight room, the pool, and all the group classes, like yoga and dance.
M: Oh, I've always wanted to try yoga.
W: The beginner class is on Tuesdays at six. You can sign up on our website.
M: Okay. I'll do that tonight. Can I fill in the form for the membership now?
W: Sure. I'll get it from the desk.

stem: Why is the man at the gym?
options: To apply for a job at the front desk.
To ask about becoming a member.
To sign up for a swimming race.
To return a student card he found.
explanation: He says 'I just started classes, and I'd like to join.' He is taking a tour and filling in a membership form.

stem: What does the man say about the price?
options: It is higher than at other gyms he has seen.
It is too expensive for a student to pay.
It includes only the weight room and the pool.
It is lower than he expected.
explanation: He says 'That's cheaper than I thought.' The woman lists the weight room, pool and group classes, so the price covers more than two things.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a nurse at the campus health center.
script: W: Good morning. What brings you in today?
M: I've had a sore throat for three days, and now I have a cough too.
W: Any fever?
M: A little last night, but I feel okay this morning.
W: Let me check your temperature. It's normal now. I think you have a cold, not the flu.
M: Do I need medicine?
W: Mostly rest and plenty of water. I can give you some throat tablets, though.
M: Thank you. Should I go to my classes tomorrow?
W: If you feel better, yes. But stay home if the fever returns.

stem: Why did the man come to the health center?
options: He needs a form for a sports team.
He wants a vaccine before his trip abroad.
He hurt his arm during a class.
He has been sick for days.
explanation: He says 'I've had a sore throat for three days, and now I have a cough too.' No injury, vaccine or sports form is mentioned.

stem: What does the nurse recommend?
options: Rest, drink water, and use throat tablets.
Take strong medicine and avoid all classes for a week.
See a doctor in the city this afternoon.
Eat more food and exercise every morning.
explanation: She says 'Mostly rest and plenty of water' and offers throat tablets. She says he may attend class if he feels better, so a full week at home is too extreme.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a cafeteria worker.
script: W: Hi, I'd like the vegetable soup and a salad, please.
M: Sure. The soup is fresh today. Do you want bread with it?
W: Does the soup have any meat in it? I don't eat meat.
M: No, it's made with only vegetables. But the bread has butter, if that matters to you.
W: That's fine. I just avoid meat.
M: Great. That'll be six dollars and fifty cents. Do you have a meal card?
W: Oh no, I left it in my room. Can I pay with cash?
M: Of course. The cash register is over there.

stem: What does the woman want to find out about the soup?
options: Whether it costs less than the salad.
Whether it contains meat.
Whether it is served with butter.
Whether it was made today.
explanation: She asks 'Does the soup have any meat in it? I don't eat meat.' The man mentions butter and freshness on his own, but those are not her question.

stem: What problem does the woman have at the end?
options: She does not have enough cash to pay.
She cannot find a table to sit at.
She forgot her meal card.
She ordered the wrong kind of soup.
explanation: She says 'I left it in my room,' meaning her meal card, and asks to pay with cash. The man says cash is accepted, so money is not the problem.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a professor during office hours.
script: W: Hi, Kwame. Please sit down. How can I help?
M: I wanted to talk about my last essay. I got a lower grade than I expected.
W: Let's look at it together. Your ideas were strong, but your paragraphs were hard to follow.
M: I see. I wrote it quickly the night before it was due.
W: That's often the reason. Next time, try writing an outline first.
M: I never do that. Is it really necessary?
W: For longer essays, yes. It helps you organize your points before you start.
M: Okay, I'll try it for the next assignment. Can I show you my outline before I write?
W: Absolutely. Send it by email, and I'll give you feedback.

stem: Why did the student come to see the professor?
options: He was disappointed with a grade.
He missed class and needs the notes.
He wants to change to a different course.
He hopes to become her research assistant.
explanation: He says 'I got a lower grade than I expected.' The rest of the conversation is about how to improve his writing.

stem: What does the professor suggest the student do?
options: Rewrite the last essay for a better mark.
Stop writing essays at night completely.
Choose easier topics for his assignments.
Plan his essay before he writes it.
explanation: She says 'try writing an outline first' to 'organize your points before you start.' She does not offer a rewrite of the old essay; her advice is for the next assignment.

text: Listen to a conversation between two students about a group project.
script: W: Chen, did you get my message about the group project?
M: Yes, I did. I'm sorry I didn't reply. The week has been crazy.
W: No worries. We need to decide who does which part. The presentation is in ten days.
M: I can do the research. I like finding information.
W: Perfect. Then I'll make the slides. Yuki said she'd practice the speaking part with us.
M: Okay, but I'm not great at speaking in front of people.
W: Don't worry. We'll practice together on Thursday. Is that good for you?
M: Thursday works. Let's meet in the study room on the third floor.
W: Great. I'll book it now.

stem: What are the speakers mainly doing?
options: Complaining about a difficult professor.
Deciding who will do each task.
Choosing a topic for their presentation.
Looking for a new member for their group.
explanation: Aisha says 'We need to decide who does which part,' and they divide the research and the slides. The topic is never discussed.

stem: What does Chen say he is worried about?
options: Speaking in front of other people.
Finding enough information for the research.
Missing the meeting on Thursday.
Making the slides look attractive.
explanation: He says 'I'm not great at speaking in front of people.' He likes finding information, and he says Thursday works, so the other options do not fit.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a library worker.
script: W: Hello. Can I help you?
M: Yes. I reserved a study room for two o'clock, but when I got there, someone was already inside.
W: Let me check the system. What's your name?
M: Hamza Khan.
W: I see it. Your booking is for room 4B, not 4A. That's probably the problem.
M: Oh, I must have gone to the wrong room. I feel silly.
W: It happens a lot. Room 4B is down the hall on the left.
M: Thanks. Do I still have the full two hours?
W: Yes, your booking runs until four. Enjoy your study session.

stem: What was the man's problem?
options: He forgot to make a reservation.
He could not log in to the library system.
He thought his study room was taken.
He arrived two hours late.
explanation: He says 'someone was already inside' the room he reserved. The worker finds that his booking was for 4B, not 4A, so he simply went to the wrong room.

stem: What can be inferred about the man's feeling at the end?
options: He is angry at the person in the other room.
He feels a bit embarrassed.
He is worried that he will lose his booking.
He is surprised that the library is so busy.
explanation: He says 'I must have gone to the wrong room. I feel silly,' which shows embarrassment. The worker reassures him that 'It happens a lot,' and his two hours are safe.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a housing office worker.
script: W: Hi, I'm thinking about moving off campus next year. Can you tell me about the apartment list?
M: Sure. We keep a list of apartments that are close to the university. Most are within a ten-minute walk.
W: Are they expensive?
M: Prices vary. A shared two-bedroom costs about four hundred dollars each per month.
W: That's less than I pay for my dorm.
M: Right, but you'll also pay for electricity and internet.
W: I didn't think of that. Can I take the list with me?
M: Of course. It's also on our website, and there's a meeting on Friday for students who want roommates.

stem: What does the woman want to learn about?
options: Housing off campus.
Rules for living in the dorm.
Ways to find a part-time job.
Prices at the campus bookstore.
explanation: She says she's 'thinking about moving off campus' and asks about the apartment list. Her dorm is only mentioned as a price comparison.

stem: What does the man point out about the cost?
options: The apartments are more expensive than the dorm.
Students must pay a full year in advance.
The rent includes electricity and internet.
Bills for utilities are paid separately.
explanation: He says 'you'll also pay for electricity and internet,' meaning the rent does not cover them. The woman says the rent is less than the dorm, so the first wrong choice is reversed.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a bus driver.
script: W: Excuse me, does this bus go to the science building?
M: Not directly. It stops at the north gate, and then it's a five-minute walk.
W: Oh. I have a lab at ten, and I'm already running late.
M: Then you should take the number eight bus. It stops right in front of the building.
W: Where can I catch it?
M: Across the street. You'll see a green sign. It comes every ten minutes.
W: Thank you. That's very helpful.
M: No problem. And next time, you can check the bus times on the campus app.

stem: What is the woman's main concern?
options: Finding her student card.
Getting to her lab on time.
Paying the correct bus fare.
Meeting a friend at the north gate.
explanation: She says 'I have a lab at ten, and I'm already running late,' so she is worried about time. Fares and friends are never mentioned.

stem: What does the driver suggest she do?
options: Take a different bus across the street.
Walk to the north gate from the next stop.
Wait for the next bus on this route.
Call the science building for directions.
explanation: He says 'you should take the number eight bus' and tells her to catch it across the street. Walking from the north gate is what this bus offers, but the number eight is faster.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a club president.
script: W: Thanks for coming to the photography club meeting, Yuki. Did you bring a camera?
M: I only have my phone. Is that okay?
W: Definitely. A lot of our members start with phones. Today we're learning about light.
M: Great. I always take my photos indoors, and they look dark.
W: That's a common problem. Try standing near a window next time.
M: I'll do that. What else does the club do?
W: We go on a photo walk every month, and in May we have an exhibition in the student center.
M: An exhibition? I'd love to show my work, but I'm not sure my pictures are good enough.
W: Everyone's welcome. Just practice, and you'll be ready.

stem: What is the conversation mostly about?
options: Buying a better camera.
Planning a trip to a museum.
A first club meeting.
Choosing a photo for a contest.
explanation: The president welcomes Yuki to the meeting, explains the lesson and tells him about club activities. Equipment and contests are not the focus.

stem: How does the man seem to feel about the exhibition?
options: Interested but unsure of his skills.
Eager because his pictures are already excellent.
Uninterested because he prefers indoor photos.
Upset that members must pay to take part.
explanation: He says 'I'd love to show my work, but I'm not sure my pictures are good enough.' That mixes interest and doubt. Nobody mentions a fee.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and an internship coordinator.
script: W: Hello, Mateo. I got your email about the summer internship.
M: Yes. I'd like to apply for the position at the city museum.
W: Excellent. Do you have your resume ready?
M: I do, but I'm not sure it's good. I haven't worked in a museum before.
W: That's okay. They're looking for someone who is curious and organized. Do you have volunteer experience?
M: I helped at a school library last year.
W: Then put that near the top. It shows you can work with the public.
M: Good idea. When is the deadline?
W: The end of next week. Bring me the resume on Monday, and I'll read it.

stem: Why does the man meet with the coordinator?
options: To report a problem at his workplace.
To ask about courses for next term.
To volunteer at the school library.
To get help with an application.
explanation: He says 'I'd like to apply for the position at the city museum,' and the coordinator offers to read his resume. His library work is only an example of experience.

stem: What does the coordinator advise him to do?
options: Apply to a different museum.
Put his library work first.
Wait until next year to apply.
Take a course about museums first.
explanation: She says 'put that near the top' about his volunteer experience, since it 'shows you can work with the public.' She wants the resume on Monday, not next year.

text: Listen to a conversation between two roommates.
script: M: Olga, are you still awake? I heard music from your room.
W: Sorry, Kwame. I didn't realize it was so loud. I'm studying with headphones usually, but they broke.
M: I have a quiz at eight tomorrow, so I really need to sleep.
W: I'll turn it off right now. Actually, maybe I can study in the common room downstairs.
M: That'd be great. It's usually empty after eleven.
W: And tomorrow I'll buy new headphones. Then we won't have this problem again.
M: Thanks. I appreciate it. Good luck with your studying.
W: Good luck on your quiz. I hope it goes well.

stem: Why does the man speak to the woman?
options: She borrowed his headphones.
She left the lights on in the hall.
Her music is keeping him awake.
She woke him up with a phone call.
explanation: He says 'I heard music from your room' and that he needs sleep before a quiz. Her headphones are broken, but he did not lend them.

stem: What will the woman probably do next?
options: Study downstairs.
Go to bed right away.
Ask the man to join her.
Buy headphones tonight.
explanation: She says 'maybe I can study in the common room downstairs.' She will buy headphones tomorrow, not tonight.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a bookstore clerk.
script: W: Hi there. Are you finding everything okay?
M: Not really. I'm looking for a notebook for my art class, but I can't find the right size.
W: What size does your teacher want?
M: The syllabus says a sketchbook, about eight by ten inches.
W: Those are in the back, next to the pencils. We have a sale right now. Buy one, and the second is half price.
M: Nice. I'll take two. One for class and one for drawing at home.
W: Do you want a bag? We charge ten cents for each one.
M: No thanks. I brought my own backpack.
W: Great. Follow me to the register.

stem: What is the man looking for?
options: A bag for his books.
A set of colored pencils.
A gift for his teacher.
A sketchbook for class.
explanation: He says 'I'm looking for a notebook for my art class' and the size is a sketchbook. The pencils are only where the sketchbooks are shelved.

stem: Why does the man decide to buy two?
options: The second one is cheaper.
The first one is too small for class.
The clerk gives him a free bag.
His teacher asked for two books.
explanation: The clerk says 'the second is half price,' and he answers 'I'll take two.' He plans one for class and one for home, so neither is too small.

text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a professor.
script: W: Professor Lee, do you have a few minutes? I missed Tuesday's lecture.
M: Sure. Was everything okay?
W: I had a dentist appointment, and I couldn't change it. I'm worried I missed something important.
M: We talked about the project for the course. The proposal is due next Friday.
W: Oh, I didn't know that. What do I need to include?
M: A short description of your idea and a list of sources. I posted the details online.
W: Thanks. I'll read them tonight. Could I ask a question about my topic afterwards?
M: Of course. Send me an email, or come by on Thursday afternoon.

stem: Why does the woman visit the professor?
options: To ask about a lecture.
To change her appointment time.
To submit her project proposal.
To complain about the lecture.
explanation: She says 'I missed Tuesday's lecture' and is worried she missed something important. She has not written the proposal yet.

stem: What does the professor tell her about the proposal?
options: It must be handed in on Tuesday.
It should be at least ten pages long.
The details are available online.
